statement: For an n=2 matrix M of independent uniform signs, P(s_min(M) <= t/sqrt(2))=1/2 for 0<=t<2 and =1 for t>=2. Consequently any bound P(s_min(M) <= t/sqrt(n)) <= t+c^n asserted for every n>=2 and t>=0 requires c>=1/sqrt(2).
assumptions: iid uniform entries in {-1,+1}; n=2; t>=0; the c condition assumes a dimension-uniform bound including n=2 with no prefactor on c^n
source: direct elementary calculation; target statement documented in Sah-Sahasrabudhe-Sawhney, On the Spielman-Teng Conjecture, Geom. Funct. Anal. 35 (2025), https://doi.org/10.1007/s00039-025-00707-z
proof: The second row equals or opposes the first with total probability 1/2, giving s_min=0. On the complementary event the rows are orthogonal and each has Euclidean norm sqrt(2), so M M^T=2I and s_min=sqrt(2). Set t=0 to obtain 1/2 <= c^2.
remaining_gap: No independent review; finite n=2 says nothing about whether the coefficient-one inequality holds for all sufficiently large n.

statement: The formula H(t)=1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is the limiting CDF as n tends to infinity for sqrt(n) times the least singular value in the real Gaussian ensemble; it is not an exact CDF for each finite n.
assumptions: G_n has iid N(0,1) entries; t>=0; the finite-n counterexample takes n=1.
source: Local C0029-A001, probability_1000_intake_claude_20260907/attempts.jsonl line 23, key_identity says 'Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t)'; Tao-Vu, Random matrices: The distribution of the smallest singular values, https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.0614, abstract says 'it converges to the same limiting distribution'; Rudelson-Vershynin 2010 ICM survey, https://public.websites.umich.edu/~rudelson/papers/rv-ICM2010.pdf, calls the expression the limiting probability.
proof: At n=1, s_min(G_1)=|Z| for a standard normal Z, hence P(sqrt(n)s_min<=t)=2Phi(t)-1. Its derivative at t=0 is sqrt(2/pi), whereas H'(0)=1, so equality fails for all sufficiently small positive t.
remaining_gap: This repairs a local source statement only; it does not decide the Bernoulli coefficient-one conjecture.
